covers: a batch removes every named task and its rows, counting a repeated name once and answering an empty batch with zeros
a batch naming a task outside the caller's scope is refused and removes nothing, so no partial delete is left behind
an unknown task name is refused, and a non-list, an empty name, a non-string entry, an over-long name or a batch over the cap is refused before anything is deleted
the earlier store, pairing, permission, diagnostics and replay cases
the same shared batch entry removes the bank tasks and their rows
a refused batch and an unknown name both leave every task and its rows intact

intentional_differences: the deployed batch delete skipped ids that are unknown or belong to someone else and reported only a count; the native entry checks the whole batch (existence and scope) before deleting, so a batch that names a task the caller may not touch deletes nothing and no partial delete is left behind
an unknown task name is refused with reconciliation.task_not_found instead of answering a zero count
the batch is capped at 200 names, where the deployed entry had no cap
the answer carries deleted, rows_deleted and the names actually removed; the deployed answer carried one count
the deployed stores are single tables with the detail inside JSONB, so deleting the task row was the whole job; the native store also removes the result rows and reports how many
the identifiers are the native CIR-/CBR- task names instead of the deployed integer ids
